title: Jersey City Heat Pump Rebates 2026: PSE&G and Electric Heat Homes
desc: Jersey City heat pump rebates in 2026 from PSE&G: $300 to $600 for homes that already heat with electricity, up to $10,000 to leave gas, oil or propane, and rules for condos and renters.
h1: Heat Pump Rebates in Jersey City
badge: $300 to $600, or up to $10,000 to leave gas
lead: Almost a third of Jersey City homes already heat with electricity, which is unusual for a northern New Jersey city. That changes which PSE&G rebate fits. A home that burns gas uses the large replacement rebate. A home with electric heat uses the standard instant rebate. Jersey City is also full of condos and rentals, where the first question is who is allowed to apply. This page was written from PSE&G's own program page, read on October 6, 2026.
cards_heading: Which heat pump rebate fits a Jersey City home
cards_intro: Each card names the fact we keep on file, with the date we last read the official page. The first card is for homes that already use electricity to heat. The next two are for homes that burn a fuel.

cards.title: Electric heat to a heat pump
cards.note: The standard instant rebate: $300 or $450 depending on efficiency, or $600 for a cold climate model. Your contractor puts it on the invoice. Baseboard and electric furnace homes can use it.

cards.title: Gas, oil or propane to a heat pump
cards.note: The lesser of $10,000 or half the project, and the lesser of $12,000 or 60% if you are income-qualified. The old system must be taken out of service.

cards.title: Keep the boiler, add a heat pump
cards.note: A dual fuel system keeps your old equipment and adds a heat pump with controls. A hybrid system that covers cooling and up to 90% of heating earns up to $2,000.

cards.title: Income-qualified bonus
cards.note: For incomes at or below 400% of the poverty level, a moderate-income area or listed benefits.

cards.title: Free home assessment
cards.note: A one-hour visit before you decide. PSE&G can install a smart thermostat and small products at no cost.

cards.title: Federal 25C tax credit
cards.note: No federal credit applies to heat pumps installed after December 31, 2025.

after_cards: All of these require that you own the house where the work happens and that the home is not new construction.
sections: Electric heat is a big share of Jersey City

The Census Bureau's American Community Survey (2020 to 2024) says electricity heats 31.7% of Jersey City homes. Utility gas heats 60.9%, fuel oil 2.6% and bottled gas 2.0%. The electric group is the group that gains most from the standard instant rebate. A heat pump moves heat instead of making it, so it can use much less electricity than baseboard heaters or a plug-in electric furnace. The savings come on your bill month after month, while the rebate lowers the purchase price once.

Jersey City's housing is only 14.4% houses, either detached (7.3%) or attached (7.1%). Another 31.5% of homes are in buildings of two to four homes. The rest sit in larger buildings or other types. PSE&G's electrification rules cover single-family and attached homes of one to four units that you own. We could not find a written rule for a condo unit in a large building, so call PSE&G at 1-855-846-2895 before you sign a contract, and ask the condo board about outdoor equipment.

Renters live in 72.1% of Jersey City homes. A tenant cannot apply for the heat pump rebates, since the program asks for the owner. If you rent, the useful moves are the free assessment, the appliance rebates and a conversation with the owner. An owner of a two- or three-family house, which is a large share of the city, can apply and may also qualify for the $300 income-based bonus.

About 29.8% of Jersey City's homes were built in 2000 or later, and 29.2% were built before 1940. Newer buildings usually have better insulation, which can make a heat pump easier to size. The oldest buildings are the ones most likely to need ductwork or air sealing first. PSE&G pays up to $2,000 for new ducts if a duct design calls for them, and up to $2,000 for taking the old equipment out. Ask the contractor to list both lines.

PSE&G offers interest-free repayment on your bill of up to $25,000 for a heating and cooling project and up to $50,000 for a stand-alone electrification project. You need 12 months of on-time payments with PSE&G, and the account holder at the property signs. Terms run 84 months, or up to 120 months for income-qualified customers on larger projects.
claim_heading: How to claim a PSE&G heat pump rebate in Jersey City
claim_steps: Confirm that PSE&G is your electric company and who owns the home.
Book the free Whole Home Energy Assessment, or call 1-855-846-2895 for a participating contractor.
Tell the contractor what heats your home now, because the rebate depends on it.
Get a written quote that lists each rebate, plus any ductwork and removal lines.
Sign the customer form after the work. The rebate comes off your invoice.
faq: I heat with electricity in Jersey City. Which rebate do I use?
The standard instant rebate of $300, $450 or $600, plus $300 more if you are income-qualified. The large replacement rebate is for gas, oil and propane homes.
Can a condo owner get the rebate?
The rules we read cover owned houses of one to four units. For a unit in a larger building, ask PSE&G first.
Do I need a participating contractor?
PSE&G says to work with one for instant rebates. Other appliance savings are available without one.
Can renters in Jersey City apply?
Not for heat pumps. The program asks for the owner of the house.
Is the federal heat pump credit available?
No. The 25C credit ended for work done after December 31, 2025.
